title: Michel B NDE 4544/944
content:
4544 Translated to English by Kathy. My NDE – Brain hemorrhage as a result of a stroke. I began answering the NDERF questionnaire on February 25, 2004, some 3 years and a few months after my hemorrhagic stroke, which happened in late October 2000. I had nearly immediate coma, surgery, resuscitation and awakening 3 weeks later. Now, in 2010 I am changing nothing to my account. Hemorrhagic Stroke occurred during the night of the 28th to October 29, 2000, around 10:30 pm. I had a feeling of discomfort while answering the telephone and an almost immediate loss of consciousness, a feeling of dizziness and the inability to speak. I mumbled a few incomprehensible words to my wife, and made some uncontrolled movements on my left side. My wife called for help (I ‘perceived’ her call). I saw a black hole. I ‘saw’ the firefighters arrive in my room. I saw a definite black hole. I underwent immediate surgery and then about three weeks in a coma during which I was on a ventilator and was given different drugs. During this time, I had a few problems with oxygen deprivation (causing hypoxia / hypercapnia (?). It may be at this time that I had my experience(s). My condition at the time of the experience was Clinical death (Cessation of respiratory, heart and brain function). I was on a respirator for 3 weeks. I don't know if I was out of body, but I had the impression of lying on a very soft, warm substance (my mattress?); it was maybe a feeling of floating. I was looking downwards, arms held close to the body. I was very, very comfortable in this extended position. I was watching as a stranger (dispassionately) the scene unfolding about 50 meters away from me. At no time did I sense fear about what was going on outside. I was at peace, totally inaccessible; a simple observer, up high but not ‘flying’. I could see both my body and the outdoors. I could see myself ‘seeing’ (very difficult to explain). I could feel no pain. I was very, very comfortable, totally relaxed, bathed in softness and light. The feeling was of light, softness, peace and an absence of fear. It is all extraordinarily difficult to describe. I saw a stranger, perhaps a nurse, or doctor, dressed in a white shirt. There was a sense of tremendous brightness, but not dazzling, to my left. The scene was taking place in the morning, quite early, and I thought I could see a radiant sun illuminating everything. I could see the scene through what I believed to be the bay window in my room. The angle was very important every time I was looking down from above on this person dressed in a white shirt covering the arms all the way to the fingers. The legs were also covered to the tips of the toes. What is notable is the luminosity that enveloped everything and the impression of peace and tranquility. The first time: The person, quite young, dark hair, stethoscope around the neck, white shirt (classic image of a doctor) very sympathetic, holding his head in his hands, is saying, ‘but it’s not possible.’ Strangely, there was no indication of worry about him. It was a strange contradiction between what he was saying and the look on his face. I could clearly hear everything that was being said despite the relative distance between the glass separating us. The second time: It was the same scene that I was observing ‘from above and without emotion’, a person (the same?) still dressed in white on the telephone saying, and ‘The first time he had one chance in a hundred of pulling through the second time, one in a thousand’. The person still had the same youthful look and I could hear perfectly clearly despite the distance (The bay window was not an obstacle) (hyper acoustics?). The sky was still exceptionally luminous but never dazzling. Each time the ‘person’ was sitting on the steps, (very clean and brilliant). The stairway had about 15 steps and led to a great hall (glass doors reflecting the sun). The hall seemed to lead to or contain something darker, but not threatening, (difficult to describe) This scenery seemed to be a type of garden or prairie, very well groomed (very green grass cut short, white and yellow flowers with very luminous colors) Absolutely nothing out of place, the impression of a great cleanliness and of life. There were no faded flowers or dead branches. This whole landscape was bathed in light, which is difficult to describe correctly. According to my later research, I believe this is something close to the Garden of Eden. I observed the scene as a stranger, with no particular emotion, except maybe the joy of being there. I was totally at peace.

out_of_body.separation_sensations_other: He reports feeling 'very, very comfortable' on a 'very soft, warm substance' and 'maybe a feeling of floating,' with 'peace' and 'absence of fear.'

tunnel.passage_other_detail: He reports seeing 'a black hole' (described as 'a definite black hole').

arrival.other_being_detail: He saw 'a stranger, perhaps a nurse, or doctor, dressed in a white shirt' (young, dark hair, stethoscope).

environment.environment_other_detail: A stairway of about 15 steps leading to a 'great hall' with 'glass doors reflecting the sun'; a 'garden or prairie' with 'very green grass cut short' and 'white and yellow flowers' with 'very luminous colors'; 'tremendous brightness, but not dazzling' and 'exceptionally luminous' sky; impression of 'great cleanliness and of life.'

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Brain hemorrhage as a result of a hemorrhagic stroke; surgery; coma with ventilator; reported hypoxia/hypercapnia during coma.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: He also reports seeing a 'black hole' prior to/around loss of consciousness.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: He reports a 'black hole' and then an observation from above of scenes (including outdoors) with intense but non-dazzling light and a garden/prairie-like setting; no tunnel-to-light, beings-of-light, life review, or boundary described.
stage_sequence.repeated_stage_detail: He describes observing the same scene twice ('The first time...' and 'The second time...').
stage_sequence.simultaneous_stage_detail: He states he could see both his body and the outdoors and could see himself 'seeing.'

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: He describes observing a scene about 50 meters away through what he believed to be a bay window, with unusually clear hearing despite the distance ('hyper acoustics?'). He also interprets the landscape as close to the 'Garden of Eden' based on later research.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “I saw a black hole.” “I was watching as a stranger (dispassionately) the scene unfolding about 50 meters away from me.” “The feeling was of light, softness, peace and an absence of fear. It is all extraordinarily difficult to describe.” “but it’s not possible.” “The first time he had one chance in a hundred of pulling through the second time, one in a thousand”.
